**The views load around what they show**

On a huge map the 3D views, the Diorama and the Render no longer try to build the whole map before they rest. A 3D view builds the land within the view distance of its camera, the nearest first, and shows the rest at most as the quick first look the 2D map gives; the Diorama builds the tiles in view and a margin around them; the Render holds and builds only the part of the map within the view distance of the point its camera looks at, and makes it again around the new place once the camera has gone far. Once what they show is ready they stop, and the processor rests. Move, and they build the new place. The Diorama and the Render also open without their second-long pause on such a map. The 2D map draws close up a map with many object layers, as WorldPainter imports them, up to 150 times faster: each image of the map went through every spot of every object layer, painted there or not, and took up to a quarter of a second on Middle-earth; it now looks only where each layer is painted, and draws the very same trees. **Settings ▸ Graphics ▸ Load** chooses between **Around the view** (the default, with a view distance of 1,024 to 8,192 blocks) and **The whole map**, as before, for flying over all of it at length. Asked for by Jack on his Middle-earth of 53,888 × 43,008 blocks.
